runtime.version_source: npm registry dist-tags.latest verified 2026-11-16 (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@motion-canvas/core); alpha 3.18.0-alpha.0 deliberately not pinned

environment_probe.detail: Motion Canvas video export is an editor websocket capture; there is no official headless CLI

headless_preflight.detail: EDITOR_EXPORT_REQUIRED: Motion Canvas exports through the editor websocket, not a headless CLI

production_gate.detail: test render is not an accepted case

facts: @motion-canvas/ffmpeg 3.17.2 is MIT and has no `bin` field in its package.json: it is a Vite server plugin plus an editor client plugin, not a CLI.
The official guide says to pick the exporter in the Video Settings tab; rendering is started from the browser editor websocket.
npm dist-tags.latest for @motion-canvas/core, 2d, ui, vite-plugin and ffmpeg is 3.17.2 (published 2024-12-14); alpha 3.18.0-alpha.0 is not pinned.
Third-party pages that show `npx mc render` are not official documentation and were not treated as a supported command.

remediation: Open the pinned editor with the prepared spec: set MOTION_CANVAS_SPEC_PATH to the prepared spec path, then `npm --prefix extensions/motion-canvas run dev`.
Open http://localhost:9000, confirm 1080x1920 / 30 FPS / sRGB and the Video (FFmpeg) exporter in Video Settings (already declared in extensions/motion-canvas/src/project.meta). Click Render.
Save the exported MP4 inside the project and run `python scripts/motion_canvas_adapter.py <project> --import-editor-export --asset-id <id> --exported-mp4 <project-relative path>`.
Only that imported, technically checked MP4 can supply render_evidence to capability_matrix(); a compile log can never do so.
impact: No real MP4 exists for this prepared job. Do not register a clip, do not supply render_evidence to the capability matrix, and do not claim a headless or verified render until an editor-exported MP4 is imported and technically checked.
